title: LSA Act s. 22B — Permanent Lok Adalat for public utility services (LSA Act s. 22B)

content.overview: Section 22B of the Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987 establishes Permanent Lok Adalats for public utility services, notwithstanding section 19. The Central Authority or every State Authority shall, by notification, establish them at places and for areas and for one or more public utility services specified in the notification. Each Permanent Lok Adalat consists of a Chairman who is or has been a District Judge or Additional District Judge or has held higher judicial office, and two other persons with adequate experience in public utility service, nominated by the Central or State Government on the recommendation of the Central or State Authority. The Authority establishing the Permanent Lok Adalat appoints them. Other terms are as prescribed by the Central Government.
content.glance: LSA Act s. 22B — Permanent Lok Adalat for public utility services (LSA Act s. 22B). Complete ADR treatise with statutory deconstruction, examples, verified authorities, forum analysis and chamber drafting.
content.study: Treat s. 22B as the establishment and composition section. Public utility service is defined in s. 22A. Cognizance, conciliation and the power to decide on merits if conciliation fails are in s. 22C, not in s. 22B. Do not collapse establishment into the award.

enhancement.definition: Section 22B requires notified Permanent Lok Adalats for one or more public utility services, composed of a Chairman of District Judge rank or higher and two experienced public-utility members.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Permanent Lok Adalats are a special forum created notwithstanding the ordinary Lok Adalat organisation power in s. 19. Their existence and composition come from notification and appointment under s. 22B; their dispute-handling powers are in the following sections.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Legal Services Authorities Act, 1987, s. 22B; definition of public utility service in s. 22A; cognizance and procedure in ss. 22C and 22D; powers in s. 22.
essentialIngredients: Central or State Authority establishment by notification
Place, area and one or more public utility services specified
Chairman: sitting or former District Judge, Additional District Judge, or higher judicial office
Two other persons with adequate public utility service experience, nominated by government on Authority recommendation
Appointment by the establishing Authority; other terms prescribed by the Central Government
enhancement.detailedExplanation: The non-obstante opening of s. 22B(1) means Permanent Lok Adalat establishment does not depend on the interval-based organisation model in s. 19. The notification controls place, area and which public utility services are covered. Composition is mandatory and specialised: a judicial Chairman and two subject members. Nomination of the two members is a government act on Authority recommendation; appointment is by the establishing Authority. A problem that asks only whether a Permanent Lok Adalat was validly constituted is answered from s. 22B and the notification. A problem about pre-litigation conciliation or a decision on merits if settlement fails must move to s. 22C and must not be answered as if s. 22B itself confers that power.
examples: A State Authority notifies a Permanent Lok Adalat for transport service in named districts.
The Chairman is a retired District Judge and the two members have public-utility experience nominated on the Authority's recommendation.
A body styled as a Permanent Lok Adalat has no District Judge-rank Chairman; s. 22B(2) composition is not met.
Parties ask the Permanent Lok Adalat to decide a public-utility dispute after failed conciliation; that question is s. 22C, not establishment under s. 22B.
enhancement.problemApplication: Check the notification, the public utility service, and the three-member composition. Stop at s. 22B if the issue is establishment. Open s. 22C only if the issue is cognizance or a decision after failed conciliation.

keyTakeaways: Establishment is by notification and is notwithstanding s. 19.
Jurisdiction is tied to notified public utility services and areas.
Chairman must be of District Judge rank or higher.
Two members need adequate public utility service experience.
Decision on merits after failed conciliation is a s. 22C question.
